claim: Vitamin C cures the common cold.
evidence: Vitamin C supplementation does not consistently prevent colds in the general population, although regular supplementation may modestly shorten their duration.

claim: Smoking increases the risk of lung cancer.
evidence: Public health evidence identifies tobacco smoking as a major cause of lung cancer.

claim: A particular herbal tea prevents diabetes in everyone.
evidence: No reliable clinical studies were identified that directly tested this specific tea for diabetes prevention.

claim: Vaccination can reduce the risk of certain infectious diseases.
evidence: Clinical evidence shows that recommended vaccines reduce the risk of their target infections or their severe outcomes.

claim: Antibiotics cure viral infections such as influenza.
evidence: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viruses such as influenza.

claim: Regular physical activity can improve cardiovascular health.
evidence: Research links regular physical activity with improved cardiovascular fitness and lower risk of several cardiovascular conditions.

claim: Drinking lemon water melts body fat without other changes.
evidence: There is no good evidence that lemon water itself melts body fat independently of overall diet and energy balance.

claim: All dietary supplements are safe because they are natural.
evidence: The safety and effectiveness of supplements vary, and natural products can still cause adverse effects or interactions.

claim: Getting adequate sleep supports health.
evidence: Adequate sleep is associated with normal cognitive, metabolic, and immune function.

claim: A newly marketed mushroom extract cures Alzheimer's disease.
evidence: The available information does not include reliable clinical evidence establishing that this extract cures Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Handwashing with soap can reduce the spread of many infections.
evidence: Handwashing with soap helps remove germs and can reduce transmission of several infectious diseases.

claim: Eating carrots allows people to see perfectly in the dark.
evidence: Eating extra carrots does not give people perfect night vision when their vitamin A intake is already adequate.

claim: A specific diet prevents every type of cancer.
evidence: Evidence does not establish that one diet prevents every type of cancer.

claim: High blood pressure often has no obvious symptoms.
evidence: Hypertension can be asymptomatic, so blood pressure measurement is needed to identify it reliably.

claim: A home remedy has been proven to eliminate all kidney stones.
evidence: No clinical evidence is provided that this particular home remedy eliminates all types of kidney stones.

claim: Seat belts reduce the risk of serious injury in car crashes.
evidence: Safety evidence shows that seat belts reduce the risk of death and serious injury in motor vehicle crashes.

claim: Taking more than the recommended dose of a medicine always works faster.
evidence: Taking more than the recommended dose can increase harm and does not reliably make a medicine work faster.

claim: A specific probiotic prevents all respiratory infections.
evidence: The evidence presented does not establish that this probiotic prevents every respiratory infection.

claim: A balanced diet can provide essential nutrients.
evidence: A varied balanced diet can supply many nutrients needed for normal body function.

claim: Detox teas remove all toxins from the body.
evidence: There is no credible evidence that commercial detox teas remove all toxins from the body.

claim: Secondhand tobacco smoke can harm health.
evidence: Exposure to secondhand smoke is associated with adverse respiratory and cardiovascular health effects.

claim: A particular supplement reverses diabetes permanently in all patients.
evidence: No reliable evidence is provided that this supplement permanently reverses diabetes in every patient.

claim: Consistent sunscreen use helps protect skin from ultraviolet radiation.
evidence: Broad-spectrum sunscreen helps reduce ultraviolet exposure when used as directed alongside other sun-protection measures.

claim: Cracking your knuckles is proven to cause arthritis.
evidence: Research has not established that ordinary knuckle cracking causes arthritis.

claim: A single blood test can diagnose every type of cancer.
evidence: Cancer diagnosis can require different tests, imaging, and sometimes biopsy; one blood test cannot diagnose every cancer type.

claim: Pregnancy requires individualized medical advice about medicines.
evidence: Medicine safety during pregnancy depends on the medicine and circumstances, so professional guidance is important.

claim: A particular fruit juice prevents malaria.
evidence: No reliable evidence is supplied that this fruit juice prevents malaria.

claim: Physical activity can support mental well-being.
evidence: Research suggests regular physical activity can benefit mood and aspects of mental health.

claim: All fevers should always be treated with antibiotics.
evidence: Fever has many causes, including viral infections, and antibiotics are not appropriate for every fever.

claim: A certain oil cures every skin condition.
evidence: The available information does not provide clinical evidence that this oil cures every skin condition.

claim: Tobacco use increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.
evidence: Tobacco use is an established risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

claim: Drinking water can prevent every kidney disease.
evidence: Adequate hydration supports health, but drinking water alone does not prevent every kidney disease.

claim: A named herbal capsule has been independently tested for effectiveness.
evidence: No study details or independent test results are supplied to verify whether this capsule was tested.

claim: Oral rehydration solution can replace fluids and salts lost through diarrhea.
evidence: Oral rehydration solution is used to replace water and electrolytes lost during diarrheal illness.

claim: Consuming sugar directly causes diabetes in every person who eats it.
evidence: Diabetes has multiple risk factors, and sugar intake alone does not inevitably cause diabetes in every person.

claim: A new wearable device detects every cancer at its earliest stage.
evidence: No validation studies are provided showing that this device detects every cancer at the earliest stage.

claim: Fluoride toothpaste helps prevent tooth decay.
evidence: Fluoride toothpaste helps prevent cavities when used as part of routine oral hygiene.

claim: All people with back pain should stay in bed until fully recovered.
evidence: For many forms of back pain, prolonged bed rest is not recommended and appropriate movement is often encouraged as tolerated.

claim: A particular food additive causes migraines in every person.
evidence: No evidence is provided that this additive triggers migraines in every person; individual responses can differ.

claim: Wearing a helmet can reduce the risk of head injury during cycling crashes.
evidence: Evidence supports bicycle helmets as a way to reduce the risk of head and brain injury in crashes.

claim: A supplement can replace prescribed insulin for everyone with type 1 diabetes.
evidence: Insulin is essential for people with type 1 diabetes, and a supplement is not an established replacement.

claim: A certain breathing technique cures asthma permanently.
evidence: No reliable clinical evidence is provided that this technique permanently cures asthma.

claim: Limiting excessive sodium intake can help manage blood pressure for many people.
evidence: Reducing excessive sodium intake can help lower blood pressure, particularly in people with hypertension.

claim: Eating late at night always causes weight gain regardless of total intake.
evidence: Weight change depends on multiple factors, including overall energy intake and expenditure; meal timing alone does not always cause weight gain.

claim: A specific app has been clinically proven to diagnose depression accurately.
evidence: No trial results or validation details are supplied to establish the diagnostic accuracy of this app.

claim: Appropriately prescribed antibiotics can treat susceptible bacterial infections.
evidence: Antibiotics can treat bacterial infections when the bacteria are susceptible and the medicine is appropriate.

claim: A cold shower kills all viruses inside the human body.
evidence: A cold shower does not eliminate viruses throughout the body or cure viral infections.

claim: A newly developed supplement reduces stroke risk by 90 percent.
evidence: No reliable trial data are provided to verify this specific claimed reduction in stroke risk.

claim: Quitting smoking improves health, even after years of smoking.
evidence: Stopping smoking provides health benefits over time and reduces risks compared with continued smoking.

claim: Taking vitamins guarantees that a person will never get sick.
evidence: Vitamins do not guarantee immunity from illness; their benefits depend on nutritional status and other factors.

claim: 0-dimensional models can simulate arterial blood pressure waveforms in patients with coarctation of the aorta.
evidence: A 0-dimensional lumped parameter model was constructed and tested against in-vivo measurements. Results demonstrate that 0D lumped parameter models accurately reproduce central arterial pressure waveforms in aortic coarctation patients before and after intervention.

claim: The 1,000 Genomes Project aims to identify genomic variants with frequencies of at least 1% in the populations studied.
evidence: By characterizing geographic patterns of human genetic variation across multiple populations, the 1,000 Genomes Project provides a comprehensive map of human genetic variation designed to discover virtually all common human variants with frequency above 1%.

claim: The 1,000 Genomes Project aims to identify genomic variants with frequencies of at least 5% in the populations studied.
evidence: By characterizing geographic patterns of human genetic variation across multiple populations, the 1,000 Genomes Project provides a comprehensive map of human genetic variation designed to discover virtually all common human variants with frequency above 1%.

claim: 10-20% of bone marrow stromal cells are donor derived after allogeneic bone marrow transplantation.
evidence: Analysis of marrow stromal populations following matched allogeneic bone marrow transplantation showed that donor-derived stromal cells accounted for between 10% and 20% of the stromal microenvironment in recipient marrow compartments.

claim: Over 50% of bone marrow stromal cells are donor derived after allogeneic bone marrow transplantation.
evidence: Analysis of marrow stromal populations following matched allogeneic bone marrow transplantation showed that donor-derived stromal cells accounted for between 10% and 20% of the stromal microenvironment in recipient marrow compartments.

claim: 40-50% of recessively inherited spinocerebellar ataxia cases are caused by a mutation in senataxin.
evidence: Screening of ataxia cohorts identified senataxin (SETX) mutations in approximately 40% to 50% of families with autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia associated with peripheral neuropathy.

claim: 60% of cases of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma contain mutations in p53.
evidence: Genomic profiling and sequencing of head and neck squamous cell carcinomas confirmed somatic alterations and inactivating mutations in the TP53 tumor suppressor in 62% of primary tumor samples.

claim: Activating mutations in BRAF are found in all melanomas.
evidence: Mutations in the BRAF gene occur in approximately 40% to 60% of cutaneous melanomas, while remaining melanomas harbor NRAS mutations, NF1 alterations, or other non-BRAF driver lesions.

claim: Adolescents with alcohol use disorders have lower prefrontal cortex volumes compared to healthy controls.
evidence: Volumetric MRI revealed significantly smaller prefrontal cortical gray matter volumes in adolescents meeting diagnostic criteria for alcohol use disorders compared to age-matched controls.

claim: Autophagy inhibition universally eliminates drug resistance across all solid tumors.
evidence: While blocking autophagy can sensitize certain resistant cancer cells, in other tumor environments autophagy inhibition produces no significant sensitization or can trigger alternative compensatory survival pathways.

claim: Intermittent fasting is more effective for weight loss than continuous daily calorie restriction.
evidence: In a 12-week randomized trial, alternate-day fasting resulted in significantly greater reduction in body weight and visceral fat compared to standard daily continuous caloric restriction.

claim: Intermittent fasting is more effective for weight loss than continuous daily calorie restriction.
evidence: A 1-year randomized clinical trial in the New England Journal of Medicine showed that among patients with obesity, a regimen of time-restricted eating was not more beneficial with regard to reduction in body weight, body fat, or metabolic risk factors than daily calorie restriction.

claim: Ginkgo biloba supplements improve memory and cognitive performance in older adults.
evidence: In a double-blind trial, elderly subjects receiving 240 mg daily standardized Ginkgo biloba extract demonstrated statistically significant improvements in short-term recall and mental processing speed compared to placebo.

claim: Ginkgo biloba supplements improve memory and cognitive performance in older adults.
evidence: The Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory randomized controlled trial involving 3,069 participants showed that Ginkgo biloba at 120 mg twice daily did not reduce the overall rate of dementia or cognitive decline compared to placebo.

claim: Glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate reduce joint pain in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
evidence: Subgroup analysis of randomized clinical trials demonstrated that the combination of glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate produced clinically meaningful reductions in joint pain and functional impairment in patients with moderate-to-severe knee osteoarthritis.

claim: Glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate reduce joint pain in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
evidence: The multicenter Glucosamine and Chondroitin Arthritis Intervention Trial found that glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate, either alone or in combination, did not reduce pain effectively in the primary overall cohort of knee osteoarthritis.

claim: Daily low-dose aspirin is recommended to prevent cardiovascular events in healthy older adults.
evidence: Low-dose aspirin therapy significantly reduces the long-term incidence of occlusive arterial vascular events and secondary myocardial infarction in aging populations.

claim: Daily low-dose aspirin is recommended to prevent cardiovascular events in healthy older adults.
evidence: Major clinical trials including ASPREE and ARRIVE showed that daily low-dose aspirin in healthy elderly adults did not prolong disability-free survival and resulted in a significantly higher risk of major gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

claim: Omega-3 fish oil supplements treat major clinical depression.
evidence: Meta-analyses of clinical trials indicate that high-dose EPA omega-3 supplementation produces significant adjunct reductions in depressive symptom scores compared to placebo in patients with major depressive disorder.

claim: Omega-3 fish oil supplements treat major clinical depression.
evidence: Large randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials found that omega-3 fatty acid supplementation did not reduce depressive symptom severity or prevent recurrent depressive episodes as standalone therapy.
